text: DEFINE changing position IS a manoeuvre THAT changes lanes OR passes another vehicle

sources.quote: Changing your position on the road involves changing lanes or overtaking and passing another vehicle.

text: DEFINE passing IS a lane change THAT moves past a slower vehicle ALSO CALLED overtaking

sources.quote: Passing is changing lanes to move past a slower vehicle.

flags.note: The handbook uses "pass", "overtake" and "overtake and pass" for the same manoeuvre.
flags.zh: 手冊對同一個動作混用 "pass"、"overtake" 和 "overtake and pass"。

text: FACT vehicles on the same road do not all travel at the same speed, even though every public road has a speed limit

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

text: FACT cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers preparing to turn are [?usually] slower than through traffic

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.
flags.zh: 保留語氣的概括說法。

note: "You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles" is motivation, not a permission, so no MAY rule is written for it.

text: a driver SHOULD start a lane change or a pass ONLY IF the driver has [?enough] space and time to complete it [?safely]

sources.quote: Before beginning, be sure you have enough space and time to complete the move safely.

flags.note: No measure of space or time.
flags.zh: 空間和時間都沒有量化標準。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle UNLESS the driver is [?sure] the pass can be made without danger to the driver or others

sources.quote: Never overtake and pass another vehicle unless you are sure you can do so without danger to yourself or others.

flags.note: Subjective certainty; no observable test.
flags.zh: 主觀的確定感，沒有可觀察的檢驗方式。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN the driver is [?in doubt]

sources.quote: If in doubt, do not pass.

flags.note: Subjective state; the catch-all behind 2.1b.
flags.zh: 主觀狀態；是 2.1b 背後的兜底規則。

text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right of the road, or to the right-hand lane of a multi-lane road UNLESS the driver is turning left OR passing another vehicle

sources.quote: Keep to the right of the road or in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads unless you want to turn left or pass another vehicle.

text: TO pass a vehicle

sources.quote: Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:
how to pass another vehicle

flags.note: Called "rear view mirror" in the night procedure (3.3.1b).
flags.zh: 夜間程序（3.3.1b）把同一面鏡子叫 "rear view mirror"。

note: Steps 1 and 2 restate the lane-change steps on the same page; the order of the steps carries "only after signalling".

steps.text: signal left AND check that the way is clear ahead and behind
WATCH FOR bicycles and small vehicles hidden in front of the vehicle being passed, vehicles turning left ahead, and vehicles or pedestrians entering from a road or driveway
signal right to return to the original lane
move back into the original lane WHEN the entire front of the vehicle being passed is visible in the inside mirror
IF the vehicle being passed speeds up THEN do not race AND go back to the original lane

text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut off the vehicle being passed by moving in front of it suddenly WHEN returning to the original lane

sources.quote: Be careful not to cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it.

text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

sources.quote: Passing within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover is not permitted.
You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.

flags.note: Stated on two pages (Changing positions, Stopping) in different words; the meanings agree.
flags.zh: 在兩個頁面（Changing positions、Stopping）用不同說法出現，意思一致。

text: a driver MUST NOT pass [?on the left of a centreline] WHEN the driver is [?30 m from] a bridge, viaduct or tunnel

sources.quote: Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

flags.note: "30 metres from" is read as "within 30 m of"; the text does not say whether it covers both approaches.
flags.zh: 把 "30 metres from" 讀成「30 公尺以內」；原文沒說是否兩端都算。

flags.span: on the left of a centreline
flags.note: Prohibits the means (crossing the centreline), not passing; passing near a bridge on a multi-lane road is not covered.
flags.zh: 禁止的是手段（越過中線）而非超車；多車道道路的橋邊超車沒被涵蓋。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN (the driver is approaching the crest of a hill OR the driver is on a curve) AND the view of oncoming traffic is obstructed AND the clear distance ahead is not [?enough] to pass [?safely]

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass when approaching the crest of a hill or on a curve where your vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed and there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety.

flags.note: No distance given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

strength_from: default (prescriptive passive "are not to be used")
text: a driver SHOULD NOT use a two-way left-turn lane for passing

sources.quote: These left-turn lanes are not to be used for passing.

flags.note: Not an imperative and no legal marker; the default puts it at SHOULD NOT, but the wording reads like a prohibition.
flags.zh: 不是祈使句，也沒有法律用語；預設規則把它放在 SHOULD NOT，但讀起來像禁令。

text: FACT pavement markings show, among other things, where it is not [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: Pavement markings divide traffic lanes, show turning lanes, mark pedestrian crossings, indicate obstacles and tell you when it is not safe to pass.

flags.note: Judgment term inside a description.
flags.zh: 描述句裡的判斷詞。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN there is a solid line at the left of the driver's lane BECAUSE a solid line there means it is unsafe to pass

sources.quote: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass. ('A' should not pass.)
vehicles travelling beside a solid yellow line

text: a driver MAY pass WHEN there is a broken line at the left of the driver's lane ONLY IF the way is clear AND there are [?enough] broken lines ahead to complete the pass [?safely]

sources.quote: A broken line at the left of your lane means you may pass if the way is clear. ('A' may pass if there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely.)
vehicles travelling beside broken yellow lines

flags.note: No distance given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

strength_from: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
text: a driver MUST NOT pass WHEN a "do not pass" sign applies to the road

sources.quote: Do not pass on this road.
a regulatory sign

note: The sign's own caption is a plain imperative; the legal force comes from the section introduction.

text: DEFINE a passing lane or climbing lane IS an added lane THAT lets slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so faster vehicles can pass [?safely] in the left lane

sources.quote: Some roads have special passing or climbing lanes. These lanes let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing and climbing lanes

sources.quote: a passing or climbing lane
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing and climbing lanes

flags.note: Judgment term inside a definition.
flags.zh: 定義裡的判斷詞。

text: FACT an advance sign tells drivers a passing opportunity is coming, AND another sign warns when the added lane is ending

sources.quote: An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing and climbing lanes

strength_from: implied ("so drivers … can begin to merge safely")
text: a driver in the right-hand lane SHOULD merge [?safely] with traffic in the left-hand lane WHEN a sign warns that the lane is ending

sources.quote: An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing and climbing lanes

flags.note: The rule is implied by a purpose clause about the sign; the text states no instruction.
flags.zh: 這條規則是從描述標誌用途的句子推出來的，原文沒有直接下指示。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

text: a driver MUST keep to the right-hand lane WHEN a "keep right except to pass" sign is posted UNLESS the driver is passing on a two-lane section where a climbing or passing lane is provided

sources.quote: Keep to the right lane except when passing on two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided.
a regulatory sign

see.figure: the "keep right except to pass" sign

text: a driver on a freeway SHOULD keep to the right AND use the left lanes for passing

sources.quote: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.
sources.where: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶1

text: a driver SHOULD use the far-left lane of a multi-lane freeway ONLY IF the driver is passing traffic that moves slower than the speed limit

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there. Drive in the right-hand lane when possible.
sources.where: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5

note: "Use the far left lane … to pass …, but don't stay there" is read as: that lane is for passing only.

strength_from: imperative ("Drive in the right-hand lane", "Get into the habit")
text: a driver on a freeway SHOULD drive in the right-hand lane WHEN [?possible] BECAUSE this leaves the other lanes clear for passing

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there. Drive in the right-hand lane when possible.
sources.where: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5

sources.quote: Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.
sources.where: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5

flags.note: No test for when it is possible.
flags.zh: 沒有說明怎樣算「可能」。

strength_from: default (stated as a description: "Most passing is done on the left")
text: a driver SHOULD pass on the left BECAUSE passing on the right can be more dangerous

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the right

sources.quote: Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the right

flags.note: The default is described, not instructed; it is needed so that 3.2.3b reads as an exception.
flags.zh: 原文是描述常態，不是指示；但要有這條預設，3.2.3b 才讀得出是例外。

flags.note: Hedged generalisation in the source.
flags.zh: 原文本身是保留語氣的概括說法。

text: EXCEPTION TO 3.2.3a: a driver MAY pass on the right WHEN the road is multi-lane OR the road is one-way OR the vehicle being passed is a streetcar OR the vehicle being passed is turning left

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the right

text: a driver SHOULD wait WHEN the driver is in the leftmost lane with a slower vehicle in front UNTIL the slower vehicle moves to the right

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the right

text: a driver SHOULD NOT change lanes suddenly to pass on the right WHEN the driver is in the leftmost lane behind a slower vehicle BECAUSE the driver in front may move to the right at the same time

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the right

text: a driver MAY drive on the right shoulder ONLY IF the driver is passing a vehicle that is turning left AND the shoulder is paved

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the shoulder

flags.note: Presupposes that driving on the shoulder is otherwise not allowed; that default is not stated here.
flags.zh: 預設「平常不能開在路肩」，但這裡沒有寫出來。

text: a driver MUST NOT pass on the left shoulder, whether or not it is paved

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.
sources.where: Changing positions › Passing on the shoulder

text: a driver SHOULD pass with [?extra care] WHEN it is night

sources.quote: Be very careful when you pass other vehicles at night.

flags.note: A caution with no named hazard, so WATCH FOR does not fit.
flags.zh: 提醒小心，但沒有指出具體危險，所以不適用 WATCH FOR。

text: TO pass a vehicle at night SPECIALIZES 2.2a WHEN the driver has to pass AND the way is clear

sources.quote: If you have to pass and the way is clear, follow these steps:

flags.note: The handbook calls the mirror "rear view mirror" here and "inside mirror" in 2.2a; both rules say inside mirror.
flags.zh: 手冊這裡把鏡子叫 "rear view mirror"，在 2.2a 叫 "inside mirror"；兩條規則都寫 inside mirror。

steps.text: switch to low beams WHILE approaching the vehicle from behind
signal, check the mirrors and blind spot, AND pull out to pass
switch on high beams WHILE alongside the vehicle being passed BECAUSE this shows more of the road ahead
move back into the original lane AND signal WHEN the entire front of the vehicle being passed is visible in the inside mirror

text: a driver SHOULD use low beams WHEN the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle UNLESS the driver is passing it

sources.quote: Use your low beams when you are less than 60 metres behind another vehicle unless you are passing it.
sources.where: Getting ready to drive › Turn on headlights at night and in poor co…

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Be patient. Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.
sources.where: Night and bad weather › Fog › DO · item 5

sources.quote: Remain calm and patient. Don't pass other vehicles or speed up suddenly.
sources.where: Night and bad weather › Fog › REMEMBER · item 3

note: The fog advice says "Avoid passing" in one list and "Don't pass" in another; both map to SHOULD NOT.

text: a driver SHOULD NOT speed up to pass a slow-moving vehicle WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Don't speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly or to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.
sources.where: Night and bad weather › Fog › Don’t · item 3

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN driving in blowing snow or a whiteout

sources.quote: Be patient. Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.
sources.where: Night and bad weather › Whiteouts › DO · item 4

text: a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass a slow-moving vehicle WHEN driving in blowing snow or a whiteout

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly or speed up to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.
sources.where: Night and bad weather › Whiteouts › DON'T · item 2

text: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR doors opening suddenly AND doors opened to load or unload WHILE passing parked vehicles

sources.quote: When passing parked vehicles, watch carefully for people suddenly opening doors or for doors opened to load and unload.

text: FACT motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds [?often] move to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions OR to be seen

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.
flags.zh: 保留語氣的概括說法。

strength_from: imperative ("Do not take this as an invitation")
text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped within its lane BECAUSE its position in the lane is not an invitation to pass (3.4.2a)

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.
how to pass another vehicle

text: a driver SHOULD change lanes WHEN passing a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a [?smaller vehicle] that is turning left ahead UNTIL it has moved to the right

sources.quote: Wait for the smaller vehicle to move right before you pass.

flags.note: The motorcycles, bicycles and mopeds turning left, named two sentences earlier.
flags.zh: 指兩句前提到的左轉機車、自行車與輕型機車。

strength_from: imperative ("do not pull up beside it")
text: a driver SHOULD NOT pull up beside a [?smaller vehicle] that is turning left ahead to make the turn at the same time WHEN the driver is also turning left, behind it

sources.quote: If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

flags.note: The source says "one of these vehicles": those named in the sentence before.
flags.zh: 原文寫 "one of these vehicles"，指前一句列出的車種。

note: Pulling up beside a turning two-wheeler is the start of a pass.

text: a driver SHOULD stay behind a [?smaller vehicle] that is turning left ahead WHEN the driver is also turning left, behind it UNTIL the way is [?clear]

sources.quote: Stay behind and turn when the way is clear.

flags.note: Same vehicles as 3.4.3b; the source only says "Stay behind".
flags.zh: 跟 3.4.3b 是同一批車；原文只說 "Stay behind"。

flags.note: No test for when the way is clear.
flags.zh: 沒有說怎樣算 "the way is clear"。

note: "… and turn when the way is clear" is written as the end of the wait (UNTIL).

text: a cyclist MAY use any part of the lane WHEN this is [?necessary for safety], for example to discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared [?safely]

sources.quote: However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:
Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

flags.note: Judgment of the cyclist.
flags.zh: 由自行車騎士自己判斷。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: A rule for the cyclist, not the passing driver.

text: a driver of a motor vehicle MUST keep at least 1 m between the vehicle and a cyclist WHEN [?practical] WHILE passing the cyclist IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

sources.quote: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.
(See Diagram 2-11.) Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.
bike lane adjacent to parking bays

flags.note: Leaves open when the 1 m minimum can be set aside.
flags.zh: 沒說什麼情況下可以不守 1 公尺的最小距離。

text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist WHEN [?possible]

sources.quote: Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

flags.note: No test for when it is possible.
flags.zh: 沒有說明怎樣算「可能」。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn [?unnecessarily] WHILE passing a cyclist BECAUSE it may frighten the cyclist and cause a loss of control

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: Who judges necessity is not stated.
flags.zh: 沒說由誰判斷是否必要。

text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly while still [?some distance] away from the cyclist WHEN the driver feels the horn must be used

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: No distance given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離。

text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right UNLESS the driver is on a one-way road

sources.quote: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

text: a driver SHOULD stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors of a streetcar WHEN the streetcar is stopped AND passengers are getting on or off

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.
a vehicle stopped the required two metres behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar

flags.note: The diagram's alt text calls it "the required two metres", which suggests a legal requirement.
flags.zh: 圖片的替代文字寫 "the required two metres"，暗示這是法律要求。

text: EXCEPTION TO 3.4.5b WHEN the streetcar stop has an area set aside for passengers

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.

text: a driver SHOULD pass a streetcar passenger area at a [?reasonable speed] AND SHOULD WATCH FOR pedestrians making sudden or unexpected moves

sources.quote: Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.

flags.note: No speed given.
flags.zh: 沒有給速度。

flags.note: The source says "these areas"; read as the passenger areas in 3.4.5c.
flags.zh: 原文寫 "these areas"，這裡讀成 3.4.5c 的乘客區。

flags.note: Repeated on the pedestrians page, with an added caution about sudden moves.
flags.zh: 行人一節重複了這條，並多一句提醒注意行人突然的動作。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in [?closely] in front of a large vehicle WHEN returning to the lane after passing it BECAUSE this reduces the space cushion the large vehicle needs to stop [?safely]

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.
sources.where: Sharing the road › Large commercial vehicles · ¶3

flags.note: No gap given.
flags.zh: 沒有給間距。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: The source also calls it discourteous.

text: a driver SHOULD allow [?more room] WHEN passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.
sources.where: Sharing the road › Large commercial vehicles · ¶3

flags.note: Comparative with no baseline.
flags.zh: 比較級，但沒有比較基準。

text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence that may affect the driver's control WHILE passing it

sources.quote: 6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.
sources.where: Sharing the road › Large commercial vehicles · ¶8

text: DEFINE a long commercial vehicle IS a double-trailer vehicle THAT can be up to 40 m long AND carries an LCV placard on its rear ALSO CALLED LCV

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length. It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.
sources.where: Signs › Other signs › Long commercial vehicle (LCV) · ¶3

sources.quote: Title: Long commercial vehicle (LCV) - Description: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)
sources.where: Signs › Other signs › Long commercial vehicle (LCV) · image

text: a driver SHOULD anticipate the extended length AND limited speed of an LCV WHEN preparing to pass it

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length. It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.
sources.where: Signs › Other signs › Long commercial vehicle (LCV) · ¶3

text: a driver SHOULD stay [?well back] of farm machinery AND SHOULD NOT pass it UNTIL it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

flags.note: No distance given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

text: a driver SHOULD keep a [?safe] following distance behind a horse-drawn vehicle AND SHOULD NOT pass it UNLESS it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Maintain a safe following distance and only pass when it is safe to do so.

flags.note: Judgment term (twice).
flags.zh: 判斷詞（出現兩次）。

text: a driver SHOULD leave [?as much distance as possible] WHILE passing a horse-drawn vehicle BECAUSE passing too closely could startle the horse and make it change direction suddenly

sources.quote: When passing, give as much distance between you and them as possible. Passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway.

flags.note: No distance given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a snow plow WHEN the snow plow is moving

sources.quote: Don't pass moving snow plows under any conditions.

flags.note: Absolute wording ("under any conditions") without a legal marker; the default gives SHOULD NOT.
flags.zh: 用了絕對的說法（"under any conditions"），但沒有法律用語；預設規則給 SHOULD NOT。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass between snow plows WHEN several snow plows are staggered across a freeway BECAUSE there is not [?enough] room to pass [?safely] AND the ridge of wet snow can throw the vehicle out of control

sources.quote: On freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow. Do not try to pass between them. This is extremely dangerous because there is not enough room to pass safely, and the ridge of wet snow can throw your vehicle out of control.
sources.where: Night and bad weather › Snow plows · ¶2

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a pilot vehicle or pace vehicle WHEN it carries the "do not pass" temporary condition sign

sources.quote: Do not pass the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bearing this sign.
a temporary condition sign

flags.span: Do not pass the pilot vehicle
flags.note: The section presents these signs as warnings, so no legal force; the wording is a direct prohibition.
flags.zh: 該段把這類標誌當作警告，不給法律效力；但用字是直接禁令。

see.figure: the "do not pass" pilot vehicle sign

text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may mean a pedestrian is crossing

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

text: FACT school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have [?illegally passed] a school bus

sources.quote: In Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus.

flags.note: Implies a prohibition on passing; the law behind it is the duty to stop in 3.4.12b.
flags.zh: 暗示有禁止超車的規定；背後的法規是 3.4.12b 的停車義務。

note: The law behind it is 3.4.12b, from the same section of the Stopping page.

text: a driver MUST stop WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, from either direction IF VIOLATED a [?heavy] fine AND 6 demerit points for a first offence

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

flags.note: The handbook says "fined heavily" and gives no amount.
flags.zh: 手冊只說 "fined heavily"，沒有給金額。

flags.note: Repeated on Sharing the road (which also counts the stop arm), the Signs page and the six-point offence table.
flags.zh: 在 Sharing the road（另把停車臂伸出也算進去）、標誌頁和記 6 點的違規表都重複出現。

note: This duty to stop is what makes passing a stopped school bus illegal (3.4.12a).

text: a driver SHOULD stop at least 20 m from the bus WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing from behind

sources.quote: If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.

flags.note: A bare imperative right after "You must stop"; it reads as part of the law in 3.4.12b, but the handbook does not say so.
flags.zh: 緊接在 "You must stop" 後的祈使句；讀來是 3.4.12b 法規的一部分，但手冊沒有明說。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT go WHEN stopped for a school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing UNTIL the bus moves OR the lights have stopped flashing

sources.quote: Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.

flags.note: A bare imperative that ends the duty in 3.4.12b; it reads as part of that law, but the handbook does not say so.
flags.zh: 結束 3.4.12b 停車義務的祈使句；讀來屬於該法規，但手冊沒有明說。

flags.span: and its stop arm is no longer activated
flags.note: Elsewhere the stop ends only when every condition holds (bus moves, lights stop, arm folds away); here either one ends it.
flags.zh: 別處要所有條件都成立（車開走、燈停、停車臂收起）才能走；這裡只要其中一個。

text: EXCEPTION TO 3.4.12b WHEN the road has a median strip AND the driver is approaching the bus from the front

sources.quote: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

text: a driver MUST slow down AND proceed with [?caution] WHEN approaching, in the same direction, an emergency vehicle stopped with red or red-and-blue lights flashing OR a tow truck stopped with amber lights flashing IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: When approaching any emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red, or red and blue, lights flashing or a tow truck with its amber lights flashing in the same direction of your travel, you are required to reduce the speed of your vehicle and proceed with caution.
sources.where: Particular situations › Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or …

sources.quote: Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle
sources.where: Keeping your licence › Table of offences › Three points · item 17

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: The offence table words it as "Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle".

text: a driver MUST move into a lane away from the stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck, [?if safe to do so] WHEN the road has 2 or more lanes in the driver's direction IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: When the roadway has two or more lanes of traffic in the same direction of your travel, you are required to move into a lane away from the emergency vehicle or tow truck, if safe to do so, in addition to reducing the speed of your vehicle and proceeding with caution.
sources.where: Particular situations › Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or …

sources.quote: Failing to move, where possible, into another lane when passing a stopped emergency vehicle
sources.where: Keeping your licence › Table of offences › Three points · item 18

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

flags.note: The offence table qualifies the same duty with "where possible" instead of "if safe to do so".
flags.zh: 違規表對同一項義務用的是 "where possible"，不是 "if safe to do so"。

text: FACT a vehicle towing a trailer cannot accelerate as quickly AND needs more space BECAUSE it is much longer

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached. Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass. Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD pass ONLY IF the driver has [?enough] time and room to complete the pass

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached. Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass. Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD allow [?more room] before moving back into the lane AND SHOULD NOT cut back in [?too soon] WHEN returning to the lane after passing BECAUSE this can make the trailer sway and become hard to control

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached. Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass. Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

flags.note: Comparative with no baseline.
flags.zh: 比較級，但沒有比較基準。

flags.note: No gap given.
flags.zh: 沒有給間距。

text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD signal, pull over AND let the other vehicles pass WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass. Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them. If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.

flags.span: If you are holding up a line of traffic
flags.note: Worded for any driver, but placed in the towing section; scoped here to towing.
flags.zh: 用字適用所有駕駛，但放在拖車段落裡；這裡限定在拖車。

text: FACT fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them that can whip a trailer to the side WHEN they pass

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass. Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them. If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.

text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT brake AND SHOULD steer the vehicle and trailer [?carefully] back into position WHEN a passing bus or truck pushes the trailer out of position

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass. Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them. If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: "A slight increase in speed may help" is a possibility, not a permission, so it stays as a note.

text: a driver being passed SHOULD move to the right AND let the faster vehicle pass [?in safety] WHEN faster traffic wants to pass

sources.quote: When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety.
5. When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:
Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.

flags.note: A sample test question says "you must" move right, and the offence table lists "Failing to share the road"; the text itself only advises.
flags.zh: 模擬測驗題寫 "you must" 靠右，違規表也列了 "Failing to share the road"；但正文只是建議。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: Two of its sources come from the sample test page (question 5); keep them out of the rule set if that page is used for evaluation.

text: a driver being passed MUST NOT speed up WHILE another driver is trying to pass BECAUSE it is dangerous

sources.quote: And do not speed up when another driver is trying to pass you. It is unlawful and dangerous.

text: a driver MUST NOT drive to prevent another vehicle from passing IF VIOLATED [?sanctions for dangerous driving]

sources.quote: driving a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing
sources.where: Losing your licence › Sanctions – dangerous behaviours · item 3

flags.note: The passage lists the behaviour but does not state its sanction.
flags.zh: 這段只列出行為，沒有寫對應的處罰。

text: a driver in [?slow traffic] MUST keep right WHEN on a multi-lane road where a "slower traffic keep right" sign is posted

sources.quote: Slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right.
a regulatory sign

flags.note: No speed given; slow compared with the traffic around it.
flags.zh: 沒有給速度；是跟周圍車流相比的慢。

note: The caption of a regulatory sign. It is the legal side of keeping right so faster traffic can pass (2.1d, 3.6.1a).

text: a driver being passed SHOULD WATCH FOR oncoming traffic AND SHOULD move closer to the right side of the lane WHEN on an undivided road AND the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

text: a driver being passed SHOULD be ready to slow down WHEN on an undivided road AND the passing driver is in the opposite lane BECAUSE slowing down lets the passing driver get back in front sooner and prevents a collision

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

text: a truck driver MUST NOT drive in the far-left lane WHEN on a high-speed road with 3 or more lanes in each direction where trucks are barred from that lane

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.
On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.
sources.where: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5

flags.note: The source says "many" such roads without saying which.
flags.zh: 原文說「許多」這類道路，但沒說是哪些。

flags.note: The Freeway page says "many freeways"; Changing positions says "many high-speed roads".
flags.zh: Freeway 頁寫 "many freeways"，Changing positions 頁寫 "many high-speed roads"。

note: A rule for truck drivers. The passing rule for other drivers (3.6.3c) depends on it.

text: a truck driver MUST use the lane next to the far-left lane for passing WHEN on a high-speed road with 3 or more lanes in each direction where trucks are barred from the far-left lane

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.
sources.where: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

text: a driver in the truck passing lane SHOULD move into the right-hand lane [?as soon as the driver can] WHEN a truck wants to pass

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

flags.span: as soon as the driver can
flags.note: No time given (the handbook says "as soon as you can").
flags.zh: 沒有給時間（手冊原文是 "as soon as you can"）。
